title: The comeback of the cassette
text: Music formats rarely get second {{1}}, but the cassette tape is an exception. Sales have {{2}} for five consecutive years, driven partly by nostalgia and partly by the appeal of a physical object in a streaming world. Bands report that cassettes sell best at live shows, where the tape {{3}} as a souvenir of the evening. Industry observers are cautious about the numbers: cassettes remain a rounding error compared with streaming, and much of the revival is {{4}} to collectors rather than listeners. Yet the cassette's limitations are exactly what some fans {{5}}: the effort of rewinding, the hiss, the necessity of listening in order. In an age of infinite playlists, constraints have become a luxury. The lesson, one label executive suggests, is that convenience does not {{6}} replace connection. Formats survive when they mean something, and meaning is the one thing the industry has never {{7}} to manufacture. Whether the cassette's comeback {{8}} depends, as ever, on the music.

gaps.explanation: 'get second chances' — the plural idiom; the singular nouns would need an article, and luck is not countable.
'sales have risen' — rise is intransitive; 'raised' needs an object, and emerge and appear mean come into view, not increase.
'the tape acts as a souvenir' — functions as one; pose as and masquerade as mean pretend falsely, and 'play as' is for football positions.
'much of the revival is attributed to collectors' — ascribed to them; donated, awarded and granted mean given, not credited as the cause.
'the limitations are exactly what some fans prize' — value highly; tolerate and endure fall short of prizing, and criticise reverses the point.
'convenience does not automatically replace connection' — by itself, as a matter of course; the manner adverbs change what is being denied.
'has never managed to manufacture' — succeeded in; 'succeeded to' breaks the pattern, afford needs 'can', and failed would reverse the sentence.
'whether the cassette's comeback lasts' — endures; collapses and evaporates reverse it, and an established revival does not arrive.
